 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/respondent No.2 challenging the judgment and award dated 11.04.2022 passed in MVC No.55/2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT-II, Yadgiri (for short,
'the Tribunal').

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Sharanamma W/O Mallappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

Appellant is respondent No.2 and the respondents are petitioner Nos.1 to 6 and legal representatives of deceased respondent No.1.
3.

Brief facts leading to rise filing of this appeal are as under:
On 04.01.2019, as per the instructions of the respondent No.1, Mallappa S/o Buggappa was proceeding in Tractor and Trolley bearing Registration No.KA-33/TA- 1769 and 1770, for unloading of stones for construction of cattle room in the filed of respondent No.1.

When they were near Shivapur village in between Yaphad to Shivapur road, at about 3.30 p.m, the driver of Tractor driven the NC:
2024:KHC-K:4921-DB vehicle in rash and negligent manner in high speed and applied sudden cut, the vehicle turned turtle.
Due to accident, Mallappa fell down from trolley and sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Government General Hospital, Yadgiri and they have referred for higher center.

On the same day,
he was admitted to Kamreddy Hospital, Kalaburagi,
He died during the course of treatment on 09.01.2019.
It is contended that the deceased was aged about 47 years and he was labour under the respondent No.1 and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

Hence,
the petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V Act'), seeking compensation on the account of death of Mallappa in the road traffic accident.
4. The respondent No.1 was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
It is contended that the deceased was traveling on the stone loaded tractor as NC: 2024:KHC-K:4921-DB an un-authorized passenger, who was a third party not covered under the policy.
Therefore, claim petition is not maintainable and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. The Tribunal, on the basis of the pleadings of the parties framed relevant issues and additional issues.
The petitioners, in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and got marked 8 documents as Exs.P1 to P8.

The official of respondent No.2 was examined as RW.1 and got marked two documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
6.
The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part.
It is ordered and awarded that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,82,602/- with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till deposit.

The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation NC:
2024:KHC-K:4921-DB amount within one month from the date of the judgment before the Tribunal.
7. The respondent No.2, aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, has filed this appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and also learned counsel for respondent No.2.

4 9.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Sharanamma W/O Mallappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that the Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability upon the respondent No.2 by overlooking the evidence of RW.1 and other documents on record.
She further submits that, the deceased was traveling on a stone loaded tractor as an unauthorized passenger.
Hence, he is not covered under third party as per Section 147 of M.V Act.
Hence, on these grounds, she prays to allow the appeal.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the NC: 2024:KHC-K:4921-DB Tribunal and submits that compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and proper.
On these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeal.
11. We have perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
The point that arises for our consideration is with regard to liability.
12. It is not in dispute that, deceased Mallappa met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries and succumb to the injuries during the treatment period.

In order to substantiate that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and trolley, the petitioner No.1 has produced certified copy of FIR marked as Ex.P1 and certified copy of the charge sheet marked as Ex.P3 which discloses that accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Tribunal was justified in recording the finding that the accident was occurred due NC: 2024:KHC-K:4921-DB to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
13. Insofar as the liability is concerned, it is the case of the respondent No.2 that the deceased was traveling on a stone loaded tractor as an unauthorized passenger.

The petitioners have contended that on the instructions of respondent No.1, the deceased was proceeding on the Tractor and Trolley for unloading stones for construction of cattle room in the filed of respondent No.1.

From the perusal of the materials placed on record, it establishes that on the date of accident the deceased was working as a Coolie under respondent No.1 and vehicle involved in the accident is Tractor and Trolley.

The Tribunal placing reliance on the judgment of this Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. MARUTHI AND OTHERS REPORTED IN (2012) ACJ 1408, held that the deceased was working as a labour and RW.1 has admitted in the course of cross examination that respondent No.2 has received a sum of - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4921-DB Rs.50/- premium amount and his risk covered under policy.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. MARUTHI AND OTHERS REPORTED IN (2012) ACJ 1408
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurance policy is a package policy and respondent No.2 cannot exonerate his liability on this ground.
The Tribunal was justified in passing the impugned judgment, as such, we do not find any error in the impugned judgment.
Hence, we decline to interfere with the impugned judgment.

14. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Miscellaneous First Appeal is dismissed confirming the judgment and award passed in MVC No.55/2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT-II, Yadgiri.
